title: OneTomorrow Donates Over $500,000 in 2022
author: Stephanie
body:
From little things, big things grow. ATGs charitable fund OneTomorrow has had an incredible year, furthering our mission as a company to have an enduring positive impact on the nature and communities we touch. We achieve our vision by promoting a more sustainable and socially aware way of travelling, by partnering with grassroots and community-led charities in the places we travel to and educating our guests on tour about their vital work.

In 2022 OneTomorrow has donated over $500,000 to our associated charities, part of which was generously donated by our guests through the OneTomorrow guest giving program. Guests can donate to their chosen partner charity and OneTomorrow will double the donation. OneTomorrow is delighted to have supported 18 charities this year, from providing specific grants, to hosting fundraising events.

Here is a snapshot of the impact OneTomorrow has had this year:

Flood Relief – Australia

We are all aware of the devastation caused to communities across Australia by the recent floods. Farmland and crops have been destroyed, and after the extreme bush fires of previous years, farmers are struggling to bounce back yet again.

As an Australian-owned business we see it as our responsibility to support our regional workers and have worked closely with organisations working to help flood-effected areas recover. Through Rural Aid, Mooroopna CFA and The Salvation Army we have donated $30,000 towards flood relief, which has been used to supply emergency accommodation and food, as well as counselling for impacted families.

Free Education – Cambodia

Travellers who have enjoyed an APT tour to Siem Reap in Cambodia will be familiar with ODA (Opportunities for Development thru Art) and the eight free schools they operate. Subsistence farming is still the way of life for many families in Cambodia, and a large number of children from regional communities end up working on farms rather than attending school.

ODA proudly helps create opportunities for children by providing free English language and computer classes in the outlying villages of Siem Reap. Being fluent in English and having computer skills are key to improving employment opportunities in the local tourism and government sector, hence lifting families out of poverty.

This year OneTomorrow donated $50,000 to support ODA’s programs, helping bringing quality education to Cambodia’s most underprivileged.

Life-changing medical treatment – Germany

ATG has been cruising through Germany for over 20 years, and have built a special relationship with Peace Village International. Peace Village International is a remarkable organisation that fly children from war-torn states to Germany to receive vital medical treatment and rehabilitation not available in their home countries. From Uzbekistan to Uganda, Peace Village International’s greatest challenge is finding appropriately equipped transport for severely injured and unwell children, which may include specifically chartered flights.

With our donation,Peace Village International were able to safely transport 123 sick or wounded children to the Peace Village, Dusseldorf where a team of physios, surgeons, doctors, and nurses were on hand to provide specialist treatment. After receiving the care they so desperately needed, all the children are also provided flights home to be reunited with their families, healthier and happier.

OneTomorrow would like to extend deepest appreciation to every ATG guest who so generously donated, as the last year proves, even the smallest donation can go a long way to improving the lives of communities the world over.
